concept.name: Execution report
concept.definition: The standard electronic message by which a broker or exchange communicates everything that happens to an order: acknowledgment of receipt, status changes, partial and full fills, cancellations, replacements, and rejections. In the FIX protocol it is the Execution Report message (MsgType = 8).
concept.intuition: It is the order's paper trail in real time - every event in an order's life shows up as an execution report.
concept.mechanics: Each report carries three state fields - OrdStatus (current state of the order), ExecType (what this message is reporting), and the transaction type - plus cumulative quantity, remaining quantity (LeavesQty), and average price (AvgPx) for the whole order chain. Reports are sent per fill and per state change and do not replace the end-of-day confirm.
concept.failure_modes: Dropped or reordered reports (sequence gaps, disconnects) leave the buy side with a wrong picture of position and open quantity, which is why session replay and end-of-day reconciliation exist. Execution reports are also point-in-time: relying on them without the final confirm invites booking errors.
concept.misconceptions: An execution report is not only a fill notice - it is also how acks, cancels, and rejects are delivered. And per FIX convention it does not replace the end-of-day trade confirmation.
concept.example: Your 1,000-share order generates three execution reports: New (ack), Partially Filled 400, and Filled with AvgPx 25.02 - together they fully reconstruct the order's life.

citations.source: FIX 4.2 Execution Report (MsgType 8), FIX Dictionary (Onix Solutions)
